title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
authors: Haobo Ma, Maksim E. Shirokov, Wenlin Zhang
abstract: It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed).   The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the identification of a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states with a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere of the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that the discrete and continuous definitions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide for all bipartite quantum states in infinite dimensions. The core mathematical technique involves demonstrating that any continuous ensemble can be accurately approximated by a countable ensemble through a recursive decomposition process. This equivalence is a major theoretical result solidifying the mathematical framework for quantifying entanglement in complex quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the mathematical coincidence between two definitions of the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) for infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum systems: the discrete version (based on countable decompositions) and the continuous version (based on Borel probability measures).
main_result: The authors prove that $	ext{E}_{	ext{d}}	ext{F}(ho) = 	ext{E}_{	ext{c}}	ext{F}(ho)$ for all bipartite states $ho$, establishing a fundamental equivalence between two ways of quantifying entanglement in infinite dimensions.
method: The proof employs a sophisticated discretization theorem, showing that any continuous ensemble can be approximated arbitrarily closely by a countable ensemble, achieved through recursive decomposition of Borel measures.
model_or_system: The system is a bipartite quantum system described by a state $ho$ on $\mathcal{H}_{	ext{AB}}$, where $\mathcal{H}_{	ext{A}}$ and $\mathcal{H}_{	ext{B}}$ are separable Hilbert spaces. The analysis heavily utilizes the mathematical structure of amplitude operators in the Hilbert-Schmidt space.
